title: Thermal vorticity and global equilibrium obstructions

items.title: Thermal vorticity and equilibrium domain
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a nonempty connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with its Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$ and length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$. Let $\beta$ be a smooth future-directed timelike Killing vector field on $O$, with components in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, and fix $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K}^{-1}$. On $O$ define

$$T:=\frac{1}{k_B\sqrt{-g(\beta,\beta)}},\qquad u:=k_BT\,\beta,\qquad \varpi_{ab}:=-\frac12(\nabla_a\beta_b-\nabla_b\beta_a).$$

Thus $T$ is in kelvins, $g(u,u)=-1$, and the covariant two-form $\varpi$ has units $\mathrm{J}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. For a smooth chemical-potential scalar $\mu:O\to\mathbb R$ in joules, set $\zeta:=\mu/(k_BT)$ and $\alpha:=-\zeta$, both dimensionless. These fields are defined only on the region where $\beta$ is future timelike; no thermal state or material realization is part of this definition.

references.title: F. Becattini, Thermodynamic equilibrium in relativity: four-temperature, Killing vectors and Lie derivatives, §§3–5, eqs. (6), (11)–(16)
Jessica Santiago and Matt Visser, Tolman-like temperature gradients in stationary spacetimes, §§III–IV, eqs. (4.1)–(4.6)
David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.4.1–2.4.5 and §4.3.1

items.title: Period of a smooth one-form along a closed curve
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $\omega$ be a smooth real one-form on $M$, and let $\gamma:[0,1]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ curve with a finite subdivision into chartwise $C^1$ pieces and $\gamma(0)=\gamma(1)$. Define its oriented period by

$$\operatorname{Per}_\gamma(\omega):=\sum_j\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))\,dt,$$

where $0=t_0<\cdots<t_m=1$ is any subdivision on whose pieces $\gamma$ is $C^1$. The covector-vector pairing is intrinsic, and additivity makes this value independent of further subdivision. No invariance under homotopy is asserted by this definition.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.3.1 and 2.4.1–2.4.5

items.title: A global potential compensator makes the contracted field exact
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian domain, let $\xi$ be a smooth future-timelike Killing field on $O$, and let $A$ be a global smooth one-form with $F=dA$. Suppose a global smooth scalar $\Lambda_\xi$ satisfies $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$. Define $\Psi_\xi:=\xi^aA_a-\Lambda_\xi$ and $\omega:=\iota_\xi F$, with $(\iota_\xi F)_a=\xi^bF_{ba}$. Then

$$\omega=-d\Psi_\xi,$$

so $\omega$ is exact. This identity uses the global potential symmetry and assumes no charged trajectory or conservation law.

references.title: Rubén O. Acuña-Cárdenas, Carlos Gabarrete, and Olivier Sarbach, An introduction to the relativistic kinetic theory on curved spacetimes, §VI.B, eqs. (262)-(268)
David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §2.4.4

items.title: An exact one-form has zero period on every closed curve
items.statement: On any smooth manifold $M$, if a smooth one-form $\omega$ is exact, so $\omega=d\phi$ for a globally defined smooth scalar $\phi:M\to\mathbb R$, then $\operatorname{Per}_\gamma(\omega)=0$ for every closed piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma$ in $M$.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete Cambridge Part III lecture notes, §§2.4.3–2.4.5

items.title: Rotation and charged equilibrium obstruction
items.statement:
Let $O$ be a nonempty connected open subset of a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with Levi-Civita connection $
abla$ and time-orientation field $N$. Let $ eta$ be any smooth vector field on $O$ satisfying $g( eta, eta)<0$ and $g( eta,N)<0$ everywhere; it is not assumed Killing, and Killing means $\mathcal L_ eta g=0$. In length coordinates $x^0=ct$, take $ eta$ to have components in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, fix $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K}^{-1}$, and let $\mu:O	o\mathbb R$ be smooth in joules. Define
$$T:= rac{1}{k_B\sqrt{-g( eta, eta)}},\qquad u:=k_BT eta,\qquad \varpi_{ab}:=- rac12(
abla_a eta_b-
abla_b eta_a),$$
and
$$h_{ab}:=g_{ab}+u_au_b,\quad D:=u^a
abla_a,\quad a_b:=u^a
abla_au_b,\quad 	heta:=
abla_au^a,\quad \sigma_{ab}:=h_a{}^ch_b{}^d
abla_{(c}u_{d)}- rac13	heta h_{ab},\quad \alpha:=- rac{\mu}{k_BT}.$$
Then $ eta$ is Killing if and only if $DT=0$, $	heta=0$, $\sigma_{ab}=0$, and $h_a{}^b
abla_b\log T=-a_a$.

In the Killing case, let $A$ be a smooth global one-form in the SI convention, set $F:=dA$, and define $\omega:=\iota_ eta F$ by $(\iota_ eta F)_a= eta^bF_{ba}$. Assume $d\omega=0$. Here exact means $\omega=d\psi$ for a globally defined smooth scalar $\psi$; for a piecewise-$C^1$ closed curve $\gamma:[0,1]	o O$, its period is $\operatorname{Per}_\gamma(\omega):=\sum_j\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))\,dt$. Let $m>0$ be a particle mass, take a nonzero constant SI charge $q_{m SI}$ in coulombs, and take $c>0$ in metres per second. For the charged Liouville ansatz $f=\exp(\zeta+g( eta,P))$ on the future massive shell from [[def-tgr-charged-liouville-data]], charged stationarity $\mathcal L_{F,q_{m SI}}f=0$ is equivalent to $ eta$ being Killing and $d\alpha=q_{m eff}\omega$, where $q_{m eff}:=cq_{m SI}$ in $\mathrm{C\,m\,s}^{-1}$ and $\alpha:=-\zeta$. Thus, in this Killing case, the equation for an unknown global smooth dimensionless scalar $\alpha$ has a solution exactly when $\omega$ is exact; any nonzero period obstructs such a solution. The scalar $\alpha$ corresponds to chemical potential $\mu=-k_BT\alpha$ in joules.

If for a constant $T_*>0$ kelvins the normalized field $\xi:=k_BT_* eta$ has a global potential compensator $\mathcal L_\xi A=d\Lambda_\xi$, then $\omega$ is exact and all its periods vanish. In Minkowski space with $c=1$, length coordinates $(x^0,r,\phi,z)$, metric $-(dx^0)^2+dr^2+r^2d\phi^2+dz^2$, time orientation selected by $\partial_{x^0}$, and $\partial_\phi=-y\partial_x+x\partial_y$, take $ eta=b(\partial_{x^0}+\Omega\partial_\phi)$ for $b>0$. The field is future timelike exactly where $1-\Omega^2r^2>0$. For $\Omega
e0$ this is $r<1/|\Omega|$, and $T=1/(k_Bb\sqrt{1-\Omega^2r^2})$ there; when $\Omega=0$, every $r$ is allowed and $T=1/(k_Bb)$. Here $b$ has units $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $\Omega$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ in the adopted length coordinates.

title: Thermal vorticity and global equilibrium obstructions — Examples

items.title: Rigid bath and nonexact electric period
items.statement: In the length-coordinate Minkowski model with $b=1\,\mathrm{J}^{-1}$, $\Omega=1\,\mathrm{m}^{-1}$, and $r=\tfrac12\,\mathrm m$, $T=2\,\mathrm J/(\sqrt3 k_B)$. On the annulus $\tfrac14\,\mathrm m<r<\tfrac34\,\mathrm m$, let $\eta=(-y\,dx+x\,dy)/(x^2+y^2)$, $\beta=b(\partial_{x^0}+\Omega\partial_\phi)$, and $F=C_0\,dx^0\wedge\eta$ for nonzero $C_0$ with units $\mathrm{T\,m}$. If $q_{\rm eff}\ne0$, then $\omega=\iota_\beta F=bC_0(\eta-\Omega dx^0)$ is closed and has period $2\pi bC_0\ne0$ on every positively oriented circle of fixed $x^0,z,r$ in the annulus. Hence no global smooth dimensionless scalar $\alpha$ satisfies $d\alpha=q_{\rm eff}\omega$.

references.title: F. Becattini, Thermodynamic equilibrium in relativity: four-temperature, Killing vectors and Lie derivatives, §5, eqs. (9), (15), and (16)
